extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/agents (practitioners handling amendments and replies)
extracted.subtask_short: amendments and replies after Office actions
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for filing, entering, and processing applicant replies and amendments to Office actions (including supplemental replies and amendments after final rejection). Guidance is primarily directed to examiners but also informs applicants/agents about allowable practices and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 37 CFR 1.135(c) (time to supply omission)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice under 37 CFR 1.135(c) of giving applicant a time period to supply an omission in a bona fide reply does not apply after a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the examiner concludes applicant is attempting to abuse 37 CFR 1.135(c) to obtain additional time (or where sufficient time remains to file the reply within the period for reply to the non-final Office action), the examiner need only indicate by telephone or Office communication that the reply must be completed within the period for reply to the non-final Office action or within any extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a) to avoid abandonment. After final, the examiner cannot give a time period under 1.135(c); applicant may obtain additional time only under 37 CFR 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the application in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal; otherwise they are not approved for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment should be denied entry if some point necessary for a complete reply under 37 CFR 1.113 (after final) was omitted. The nature of the omission (e.g., whether the amendment raises new issues, or would place the application in condition for allowance but for being unsigned or not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121) is immaterial; the examiner cannot give time under 1.135(c) to supply the omission after final. Examiner has discretion to enter replies, withdraw finality, and issue new actions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment authorization when reply substantially places application in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply to a final Office action substantially places the application in condition for allowance, an examiner may request that the applicant authorize an examiner's amendment to correct the omission and place the application in condition for allowance; the date of the reply is the date of such authorization (not the date the incomplete reply was filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may also enter the reply, withdraw finality of the last Office action, and issue a new Office action (non-final, final if appropriate, or action closing prosecution under Ex parte Quayle). These courses are within examiner discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 7.95 for bona fide non-responsive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.95 should be used where a bona fide reply to a non-final Office action is not fully responsive; it gives applicant ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS from mailing to supply the omission or correction to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of this time period may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Examiner Note: practice does not apply where there has been a deliberate omission or where application is subject to a final Office action; examiner has no authority to grant an extension if the period for reply has expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to present arguments (form paragraph 7.95.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should submit an argument under the heading 'Remarks' pointing out disagreements with the examiner's contentions and must discuss references applied against the claims, explaining how the claims avoid or distinguish from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.95 and is intended primarily for use in pro se applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.111 supplemental replies limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply supplemental to a reply that is in compliance with 37 CFR 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right except when clearly limited to specific categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may enter a supplemental reply if it is clearly limited to: (A) Cancellation of claim(s); (B) Adoption of examiner suggestion(s); (C) Placement of the application in condition for allowance; (D) Reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply was filed; (E) Correction of informalities (e.g., typographical errors); or (F) Simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply will be entered if filed within the period during which action is suspended under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c). The list is not exhaustive and examiner discretion may allow other supplemental replies; non-compliant amendments under 37 CFR 1.121 will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to file fully responsive first reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to include a complete, fully responsive reply in compliance with 37 CFR 1.111(b) in the first reply to prevent need for supplemental replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental replies will not be entered as a matter of right except when filed within a suspended period. Submission of a supplemental reply will cause a reduction of any accumulated patent term adjustment under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(8). If not entered, applicant should include changes in the next reply; applicant cannot simply request entry in the subsequent reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.147 to notify supplemental reply not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may use form paragraph 7.147 to notify applicants that a supplemental reply is not approved for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 provide the date Office received the supplemental reply; in bracket 2 insert reason for non-entry as noted in 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2)(i), e.g., 'The supplemental reply is clearly not limited to placement of the application in condition for allowance.' Do not use this paragraph if supplemental reply has been entered; use PTOL-326 or PTOL-37 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-responsiveness of supplemental reply received after mail date
rubrics_metrics.description: If a supplemental reply is received after the mail date of an Office action and is not responsive to that Office action, the Office will not mail a new Office action responsive to that supplemental reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a courtesy, applicant may be notified that the supplemental reply is nonresponsive and that a timely responsive reply must be filed to avoid abandonment. See MPEP § 714.05 for cross-in-mail situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims added without pointing out patentable novelty should not be allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: In amended cases where no attempt is made to point out the patentable novelty, the claims should not be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment failing to point out the patentable novelty that applicant believes the claims present may be held not fully responsive and a time period set to furnish a proper reply if statutory period has expired or nearly so. If claims as amended are clearly open to rejection on the record, a final rejection should generally be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate inspection of actions filed near end of reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions by applicant filed near the end of the period for reply should be inspected immediately upon filing to determine whether they are completely responsive to the preceding Office action to prevent abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If found inadequate and sufficient time remains, applicant should be notified of deficiencies and warned to complete the reply within the period. See MPEP § 714.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist for amended applications (items to inspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amended applications forwarded to the examiner should be inspected at once to determine signature, filing within statutory period, full responsiveness and compliance with 37 CFR 1.121, whether changes warrant transfer, special status, interference-related copied claims, traversal of restriction requirement, use of permanent ink, cited references, terminal disclaimer, or added security matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to specific MPEP sections: signature (§ 714.01(a)), statutory period (§ 710 - § 710.05), responsiveness (§ 714.03 and § 714.04), transfer (§ 903.08(d)), special (§ 708.01), interference issues (Chapter 2300), restriction traversal (§ 818.03(a)), permanent ink (§ 714.07), cited references (§ 707.05(b) and § 1302.12), terminal disclaimer (§ 804.02, § 804.03, § 1490), security (§ 115).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental action when amendment crosses in mail
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental action may be necessary when an amendment is filed on or before the mailing date of the regular action but reaches the Technology Center later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental action should specify which portions of the previous action are to be disregarded and point out that the period for reply runs from the mailing of the supplemental action. The action should be headed 'Responsive to amendment of (date) and supplemental to the action mailed (date).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent ink requirement for amendments (37 CFR 1.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires 'permanent dark ink or its equivalent' on papers which will become part of the record; documents on 'easily erasable' paper violate the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If noncompliance is discovered early, applicant is promptly notified that amendment is not entered and required to file a permanent copy within 1 month or authorize the PTO to make a copy at applicant expense. If no appropriate reply, PTO makes a copy and charges applicant. If discovered later when application is reached for action, similar steps are taken but action is not held up; requirement for permanent copy is included in Office action. Good photocopies or fax on satisfactory paper may be acceptable; see MPEP § 608.01 for acceptable copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required to pay excess claims fees for each claim that is in excess of 3 in independent form or in excess of 20 (whether dependent or independent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for a proper multiple dependent claim are calculated based on the number of claims to which the multiple dependent claim refers (37 CFR 1.75(c)) and a separate fee is required in each application containing a proper multiple dependent claim. When applicant adds a new excess claim that is in excess of the number of claims previously paid for (after considering canceled claims), applicant must pay required excess claims fees before the examiner considers the new claim. Example provided in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.116 — amendments and evidence after final
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment after final action must comply with 37 CFR 1.114 or 37 CFR 1.116; after final rejection, an amendment may be made canceling claims or complying with form requirements, may present rejected claims in better form for appeal, or may be admitted touching the merits upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission or refusal to admit amendments after final does not relieve the application from appeal condition or abandonment rules. Special restrictions apply to inter partes and ex parte reexamination proceedings (see subsections (c)-(g) in 1.116). Affidavits or other evidence submitted after final may be admitted upon showing good and sufficient reasons (1.116(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies after final limited to 1.116 amendments, appeal, or RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 (after final) is limited to: (A) an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.116; (B) a Notice of Appeal (and appeal fee); or (C) a request for continued examination (RCE) filed under 37 CFR 1.114 with a submission meeting 37 CFR 1.111 and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 1.114 does not apply to utility or plant patent applications filed before June 8, 1995 and design applications. Further avenues include CPA for design applications per 1.53(d) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b)(3) for amendments after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where an amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or otherwise requires only cursory review, compliance with the requirement of a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b)(3) is expected in all amendments after final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit or other evidence filed after final rejection but before or on same date of filing appeal may be entered upon showing of good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented; see 37 CFR 41.33 and MPEP § 1206 for post-appeal affidavits/evidence procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter amendment should not be arbitrary; must identify new matter or explain further consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed amendment does not place the case in better form for appeal nor in condition for allowance, applicant should be promptly informed and the refusal to enter should not be arbitrary; the proposed amendment should be given sufficient consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment raises the issue of new matter, the examiner should identify the subject matter that would constitute new matter. If it presents new issues requiring further consideration/search, provide explanation. Reasons for non-entry should be concise. Examples of reasons: (A) amendment would not avoid rejections; (B) amendment would raise issue of new matter; (C) amendment presents new issues requiring further search; (D) amendment presents additional claims without canceling finally rejected claims and thus not placing application in better condition for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate status of each claim and which proposed claims would be entered on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should indicate the status of each claim of record or proposed in the amendment, and which proposed claims would be entered on the filing of an appeal if filed in a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever an amendment is entered for appeal purposes, the examiner must indicate on the advisory action which individual rejection(s) set forth in the action from which the appeal was taken would be used to reject the new or amended claim(s). Use form PTOL-303 and form paragraph 7.169 when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Advisory Action PTOL-303 for replies after final prior to appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Action Before the Filing of an Appeal Brief (PTOL-303) should be used to acknowledge receipt of a reply from applicant after final rejection where such reply is prior to filing an appeal brief and does not place the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form advises applicant of disposition of proposed amendments and the effect of any argument or affidavit not placing the application in condition for allowance or which could not be made allowable by a telephone call to clear up minor matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness expectations for examiner processing of amendments after final
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner is expected to turn in a response to an amendment after final rejection within 10 calendar days from the time the amendment is received by the examiner; a reply to an amendment after final rejection should be mailed within 30 days of the date the amendment is received by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In all instances where an application is placed in condition for allowance, applicant should be notified promptly of allowability by Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37). If delays in processing the Notice of Allowability are expected, the examiner should notify applicant by interview and mail PTOL-413B Examiner Initiated Interview Summary. Prompt notice can avoid unnecessary appeal and abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period language and calculation of extension fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rejections must include specific wording setting a shortened statutory period for reply to expire three months from the date of the action and explaining how advisory action timing affects the shortened period and calculation of extension fees; in no event may the statutory period extend beyond six months from the date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant initially replies within 2 months and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the end of the 3-month shortened period, the period for reply for computing extension fees is the date the advisory action is mailed, but never later than six months from the final action date. If first reply is not filed within 2 months, extension fees per 37 CFR 1.136(a) are calculated from end of reply period set in the final rejection. Failure to file during shortened statutory period results in abandonment unless extended under 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on applicant rights after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered, applicant no longer has any right to unrestricted further prosecution; applicant cannot as a matter of right amend finally rejected claims, add new claims after a final rejection (see 37 CFR 1.116) or reinstate previously canceled claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further examination may be obtained via RCE (1.114) or CPA (1.53(d)) where applicable; amendments that merely cancel claims, adopt examiner suggestions, remove issues for appeal, or otherwise require only cursory review are exceptions. The U.S. PTO does not recognize 'conditional' authorizations to charge an appeal fee; any conditional authorization to charge an appeal fee will be treated as unconditional payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of no appeal or no timely amendment after final
rubrics_metrics.description: If no appeal has been filed within the period for reply and no amendment has been submitted to make the application allowable or which can be entered in part, the application stands abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a 37 CFR 1.181 petition will not stay the period for reply (37 CFR 1.181(f)). See MPEP § 1206 for appeal and post-appeal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.169 — Advisory Action, Proposed Rejection of Claims, Before Appeal Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.169 may be used to notify applicant in the Advisory Action that the proposed amendment(s) will be entered upon appeal and how the new or amended claim(s) would be rejected; specifies identification of claims and rejections for the Examiner's Answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 identify all new or amended claims that would be grouped in a single rejection; in bracket 2 identify the rejection by referring to paragraph number or statement of rejection in the final Office action; repeat paragraph for each group of claims subject to same rejection; use when PTOL-303 indicates proposed amendment(s) will be entered upon appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited procedure for processing amendments and replies under 37 CFR 1.116
rubrics_metrics.description: To take advantage of expedited processing, the amendment or other reply under 37 CFR 1.116 must be marked 'Reply under 37 CFR 1.116 — Expedited Procedure - Technology Center (Insert Technology Center Number)' on the upper right of the paper and the envelope marked 'Mail Stop AF' in lower left; envelope should contain only replies under 1.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings preferably written in bright color with a felt point marker. If mailed, send to 'Mail Stop AF, Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia, 22313-1450.' The reply may alternatively be hand-carried to the Customer Window. The outside of the envelope should be similarly marked. Hand-carried papers for TCs may only be delivered to the Customer Window (address provided).
